text:
sara: follow-up from the CP separation spike 1 - proposal: present an opaque control-plane surface for private customers. CP should never surface region/AZ identifiers in metadata. instead we give logical endpoint handles and let regional relays map those to infra. pros/cons?

michael: when you say "opaque" do you mean completely hiding region info from customers and support UIs, or just hiding it from API responses?

sara: both. API responses return logical names only (e.g., endpoint.redwood.net/t-xyz/ep-999). console shows locality hints rather than provider region names. support can request relay logs via a signed, short-lived token but CP UI won't show explicit region strings.

lee: how do we do routing and compliance pinning? some customers need strict region placement.

sara: explicit affinity remains opt-in in tenant config. default = opaque. sample config: ```yaml
private_endpoints:
  affinity_mode: opaque # | explicit
  explicit_affinities:
    - endpoint: ep-999
      region: us-east-2
```

carol: quotas/rls: CP won't know where traffic hits, so how enforce per-region throttles or outage mitigation?

michael: enforce at relays. CP is SOT for quota amounts and issues short-lived quota-lease blobs to relays. relays enforce locally and report back aggregated usage. lease example (treated as opaque string by CP consumers): ```json
{"lease_id":"L-abc","tenant":"t-xyz","tokens":5000,"ttl":"PT5M"}
```

sara: relay leases also allow continued serving for short windows if CP unreachable. we must define TTLs carefully. proposed defaults: quota-lease ttl=5m, leader-lease ttl=60s, relay heartbeat=30s.

lee: risk: split-brain during relay cutovers. two relays might accept the same tenant mapping. need deterministic leader election and renewal semantics.

carol: agree. CP should sign leader leases per (tenant,relay). renewal must be single writer per tenant mapping. signed-leader token example (opaque): ```text
LEADER|relay-17|t-xyz|exp=1710000000|sig=...
```

sara: ops implications: relays create VPC attachments and route table entries. CP only sends "intent" (logical attach/unattach). relays translate to provider APIs. route cleanup must be idempotent and tolerant of partial failures.

michael: operator tooling: provide a relay-audit command that lists active logical attachments and their provider state, but redact region names unless support-authorized.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: sara/opaque-cp-surface staged rollout to relays relay-12,relay-13 at 2026-04-10T09:22:00Z :white_check_mark:

sara: rollout plan: canary 50 tenants on relay-12/13 for 48h, simulate CP outage (15m) and quota exhaustion tests. if stable, expand to 10% tenants. docs: RFC addendum + operator runbook + customer FAQ (language for "locality hint").

lee: testing note: include a cross-relay takeover test where leader lease renewal is delayed and verify demotion + reattachment flows are safe. also test route table garbage collection on rapid attach/detach churn.

carol: support flow: customer sees "locality: proximate" or "locality: remote" in console. if they escalate, support can generate a signed relay-log token (5m TTL) which allows relay to return verbose logs for that request id. we should audit and require approval for >5 log downloads/day per tenant.

michael: metrics: surface latency p50/p95/p99 per-logical-endpoint, success rates, and relay heartbeat status. hide cloud-region tags, instead use anonymized locality buckets (A,B,C).

sara: next actions: 1) draft RFC addendum with leader-lease semantics + lease TTLs 2) implement relay debug token flow spike 3) operator runbook for relay demotion/cutover 4) run canary (50 tenants) 48h and run failure-mode scenarios.

carol: +1. I'll start the runbook and the customer FAQ.

lee: +1. will add the takeover unit tests to the relay integration suite.

sara: if no objections I'll drop the addendum into rfc/networking by EOD. :thumbsup:
